question: Should OpenClaw establish a single enforced validation contract for Markdown injected into model context, and if so should violations block loading, warn and annotate context, or be handled by a narrower trust/isolation design?
rationale: The request spans user-owned workspace files, local skills, native ClawHub flows, and publish-side policy. Selecting enforcement and upgrade behavior changes the product security boundary and cannot be safely inferred from the existing code scanner alone.

options.title: Define a shared prompt-content contract
options.body: Specify common rule classes, diagnostics, default enforcement, documented override behavior, and every ingestion/publish boundary before assigning a bounded implementation.

options.title: Narrow to transparent validation
options.body: Limit the first milestone to explicit metadata and parse diagnostics for workspace skills, leaving prompt-injection enforcement to a later security design.

options.title: Pursue instruction isolation instead
options.body: Adopt a broader trust-separation design through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12512 and treat content linting only as supplemental detection.

recommendation.title: Define a shared prompt-content contract
recommendation.body: Specify common rule classes, diagnostics, default enforcement, documented override behavior, and every ingestion/publish boundary before assigning a bounded implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue discussion and adjacent current-main history show the clearest cross-boundary ownership signal.
